--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 08 November, 2026
TO: Coaching Institute / Academy
RE: Rebuttal against deduction / refund rejection notice for INR 140,000/-

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am in receipt of your communication regarding the deduction/refusal of my refund of INR 140,000/-.

Please be advised that your stated grounds are legally untenable:
1. Under Indian law (Transfer of Property Act Sec 108(m) / Consumer Protection Act 2019 Sec 2(46)), standard boilerplate clauses and arbitrary deductions without verified third-party contractor tax invoices are legally void as unfair terms.
2. In the absence of documented mutual inspection reports and verifiable GST invoices, any unilateral withholding constitutes unauthorized retention and unjust enrichment.

I reiterate my formal demand for the immediate release of INR 140,000/- within 7 days, failing which this matter will be escalated to the National Consumer Helpline (1915) and the competent District Consumer Commission without further notice.

Sincerely,
[Complainant Name]

pillar_4_help_them_argue.objection: You signed the admission form acknowledging that fees once paid is strictly non-refundable under any circumstances. We cannot make an exception.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.intent: Citing one-sided boilerplate contract to withhold advance tuition.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.suggested_rebuttal: The Supreme Court of India and NCDRC in landmark judgments including FIITJEE vs Minathi Nayak have explicitly held that educational institutions cannot hoard advance fees if a student withdraws mid-way. Under the CCPA Coaching Guidelines 2024 and Section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, a 'no refund' clause is void as an Unfair Contract. You are legally required to refund the pro-rata unutilized fee within 10 days.
